title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## PAC-MAN: Humanoid Dodgeball Safety

### The Breakthrough
The authors introduce PAC‑MAN, a framework that fuses control‑barrier functions with reinforcement learning while relying only on segmentation‑masked depth from a head‑mounted camera. The system learns evasive reflexes via an adversarial motion prior and deploys a lightweight Link‑CBF policy zero‑shot on a real Unitree G1 robot, achieving 95% throw‑evasion success in a simulated dodgeball benchmark transferred to hardware.

### The Caveats
The 95% success rate is demonstrated on a single Unitree G1 robot in a narrow dodgeball scenario, with no broader real‑world tests to confirm generality.

## FA-RDP: Frequency‑Adaptive Diffusion Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
FA‑RDP is a diffusion‑based policy that switches inference frequency during a manipulation episode: a multi‑frequency visual‑force Transformer predicts low‑frequency multi‑step actions before contact and high‑frequency one‑step actions after contact, guided by a learned multimodality indicator and Manifold Consistency Distillation. Experiments on three contact‑rich tasks report the highest success rates among baselines while preserving diverse pre‑contact trajectories.

### The Caveats
The paper reports top success rates yet provides no named or described baselines, making its performance advantage impossible to verify.

## X-NavDP: Generalized Navigation Diffusion

### The Breakthrough
The X‑NavDP framework adds Group Q‑score Reweighted Matching (GQRM) to a diffusion‑RL policy, introducing self‑bootstrapped exploration with behavior perturbation and per‑trajectory Q‑score normalization. Distributed online RL across heterogeneous robots lifts success‑rate from 61.20% to 84.28% in simulation and from 10% to 65% on hard real‑world navigation cases.

### The Caveats
The paper reports large success‑rate gains but never benchmarks against existing navigation baselines, leaving true comparative performance unclear.

## TEA-AgriVLN: Traversability Alerts for Agricultural VLN

### The Breakthrough
TEA‑AgriVLN adds a Traversability Estimation Alarm that predicts per‑pixel traversability from camera images and forces the navigation policy to reconsider mismatched actions. Integrated with the AgriVLN backbone, it raises Success Rate from 0.47 to 0.54 and cuts Navigation Error from 2.91 m to 2.70 m on the A2A benchmark.

### The Caveats
Results are confined to a single simulated A2A benchmark with no real‑world robot experiments, so the claimed state‑of‑the‑art performance may not hold on actual agricultural hardware.

## AMD MI355X Beats NVIDIA B300 for Kimi K3 Inference

### The Breakthrough
By fixing a missing top‑k renorm function and adding a head‑count zero‑padding prefill kernel, speculative decode speed improves ~2.2× and cold‑prefill throughput rises ~2.3×, enabling the MI355X GPU to run the 2.8‑trillion‑parameter Kimi K3 model at ~952 tokens/s per node—about 2.4× cheaper per GPU‑hour than comparable NVIDIA B300 nodes.

### The Caveats
The performance‑per‑dollar claim rests solely on token‑throughput numbers, with no measurements of power consumption, downstream task quality, or real‑world latency.

## Episko: Rust Cockpit for Claude Code Agents

### The Breakthrough
Episko aggregates Claude Code agents into a single Rust‑based UI, auto‑discovering project scripts and displaying Git metadata alongside session cost analytics, and predicts future spend over 5‑hour and 7‑day windows to help users stay within token limits.

### The Caveats
The tool is presented without any user studies, performance benchmarks, or independent testing, so its claimed benefits remain unverified.

### Priority
PAC‑MAN provides a complete, hardware‑validated safety pipeline that can be adopted today to make humanoid robots operate safely with limited perception.

### One action
Start by adding a lightweight control‑barrier‑function safety layer to your existing RL controller, using depth‑masked perception if available.

### What to watch
Both FA‑RDP and X‑NavDP push diffusion‑based policies toward real‑world adaptability: FA‑RDP focuses on frequency‑adaptive control for contact‑rich manipulation, while X‑NavDP introduces group Q‑score reweighting to generalize navigation across embodiments. Watching how each handles the trade‑off between diversity and reactivity will reveal broader patterns for diffusion policies in embodied AI.
